profiles.meeting_scenario: NordVale Metals, a mid-sized industrial recycling company, is preparing a board pre-read for a proposed battery black-mass recycling facility in Lodz, Poland. The investment is being framed with a real-options approach rather than a standard DCF because the project has two staged commitments: an initial pilot phase and a later scale-up decision once recovery yields and offtake traction are clearer. This planning meeting is between Strategic Finance and Corporate Development to decide how the analysis will be built, what assumptions and supporting materials will be used, who will own each workstream, and what will be delivered before the board packet deadline in three weeks. The agenda is to confirm the modeling structure, source assumptions for the base case, define the deliverable package, assign responsibilities, and set the review cadence. The expected outcome is an apparently shared plan for a board-ready valuation package with a binomial-tree model, Project VaR support, and a timeline for internal review.

members.name: Elena Morozova
members.expertise: Capital allocation, valuation, risk modeling, real-options analysis
members.background: Former infrastructure valuation lead at a global bank; joined NordVale three years ago to modernize investment appraisal for large industrial projects.
members.private_state: She wants this project to become the internal proof point that real-options modeling can be practical and analytically defensible without creating a long, resource-heavy modeling cycle; she is especially concerned that excessive presentation work or cross-functional rewrites will delay the finance case.
hidden_assumptions: For major capex work, the 'base case' automatically means Treasury's latest quarterly price-and-FX deck because Finance treats that as the default planning curve once it is published.

The 'pilot stage' for this project means the company-funded demonstration line, site preparation, and permitting package in Lodz; outsourced tolling trials happened earlier and are not part of the option tree.

A package is 'board-ready' once the valuation logic, assumptions, and downside support are complete enough for the CFO and Finance Committee to defend; formatting and broader narrative can be layered on afterward.

The 'standard Project VaR appendix' means the one-page Finance format using Gaussian cash-flow uncertainty and a closed-form 95% project value calculation, because that is the only version her team keeps as a reusable template.

members.name: Daniel Reed
members.expertise: Board materials, investment narratives, strategic partnerships, deal process management
members.background: Former strategy consultant and in-house corporate development manager; he now shepherds strategic investments from concept through board approval and external partner coordination.
members.private_state: He wants a clean, persuasive recommendation that the board can approve without reopening market assumptions or getting distracted by technical finance details; he is worried that a model-first process will produce something correct but not decision-ready.
hidden_assumptions: For strategic initiatives, the 'base case' means the annual-plan market deck used at the January strategy offsite, because that is the version the board has already seen and mentally anchored on.

The 'pilot stage' means a limited commercial test through NordVale's tolling partner in southern Poland before any owned equipment is committed; that is the first real decision point he expects the board to consider.
A package is 'board-ready' only when it is a polished full-board pre-read with recommendation language, visuals, and enough cross-functional buy-in that directors will not ask for a second round.

The 'standard Project VaR appendix' means the Strategy Office's narrative-heavy risk appendix from last year's specialty-alloys deal, which included Monte Carlo fan charts and management-action commentary rather than a purely analytic finance page.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both repeatedly refer to 'the pilot stage' as the first option step in the plan.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the owned demonstration line in Lodz, including initial plant capex, site prep, and permitting costs that form Stage 1 of the binomial tree.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the outsourced tolling-partner commercial test, with no owned equipment yet, after which NordVale would decide whether to fund the demonstration line.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both regard 'pilot' as a familiar internal shorthand and each assumes the other is naturally using the same company vocabulary; because both versions are plausibly 'early-stage testing,' the divergence hides behind apparently smooth agreement.

misalignment_points.topic: Which assumptions are in the 'base case'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to build the analysis off 'the base case' without naming the underlying deck.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to Treasury's Q2 2026 commodity-price and EUR/USD curve file released last week, which Finance treats as the current official planning set.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the January annual-plan market-demand and pricing deck that was used in the board strategy offsite and already appears in prior board materials.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In many companies 'base case' is treated as singular and self-evident, so neither expects that more than one legitimate default exists; both also assume they are reducing confusion by using the standard phrase rather than restating the file name.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they need a 'board-ready' package by the deadline.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a finance-defensible package: completed real-options model, assumptions list, downside support, and enough explanation for the CFO and Finance Committee to review.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the full board pre-read: polished recommendation memo, visuals, cross-functional endorsements, and wording suitable for immediate circulation to directors.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a shared business milestone, and both assume the other knows the normal maturity level expected before board circulation; because neither wants to seem procedural or pedantic, they do not unpack the threshold.

misalignment_points.topic: What the 'standard Project VaR appendix' contains
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to include 'the standard Project VaR appendix' in the pack.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a one-page Finance appendix using Gaussian uncertainty assumptions and a closed-form 95% Project VaR linked directly to the binomial-tree valuation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the Strategy Office appendix style used last year: Monte Carlo fan charts, scenario narration, and management-action commentary designed for board readability.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both teams have previously circulated something called a 'Project VaR appendix,' each assumes there is a common house template; the phrase signals routine execution, so neither feels a need to describe the actual format or method.
